title: Indices basics
subtitle: Understand what powers mean and how to calculate them.

explanation.title: What does an index tell us?
paragraphs: An index is the small raised number next to a base. It tells you how many copies of the base to multiply together. An index is also called an exponent.
In 4³, the base is 4 and the index is 3. Write three 4s, then multiply them together.
We read 4³ as “four to the power of three” or “four cubed”. It means 4 × 4 × 4, not 4 × 3.
An index of 2 is called “squared”: 6² = 6 × 6 = 36. An index of 3 is called “cubed”: 3³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
key_points: The base tells you which number to repeat.
The index tells you how many copies to multiply together.
The value is the result of the multiplication.
Squared means two copies; cubed means three. Do not multiply the base by the index.

interactive.title: Build a power one factor at a time
interactive.intro: Grow 2 into a power by adding one factor at a time, then check what you've built.

worked_examples.title: 4³ is not 4 × 3
steps: The index 3 means three 4s multiplied together, not "4 times 3".

worked_examples.title: Why 6² is "six squared"
steps: "Squared" just names a power of 2. It does not mean ×2.

worked_examples.title: Why 3³ is "three cubed"
steps: "Cubed" just names a power of 3. It does not mean ×3.

worked_examples.title: Write 8 × 8 using an index
steps: Count how many times 8 appears: twice.
Two factors of 8 means an index of 2.

question_bank.title: Practise indices
question_bank.intro: Identify the base and index, expand powers, calculate values, and convert both ways.
